Public attention to economic inequality has grown a lot over the last twenty years. At the same time, the available data has greatly improved too: it now covers many more countries and longer time periods, and is more comparable and accessible than ever.

We’ve just published a new topic page on economic inequality to help make the data easier to understand.

It covers three key international datasets, each offering a different perspective: the World Inequality Database, the Luxembourg Income Study, and the World Bank’s Poverty and Inequality Platform.

The World Bank data, for example, is a crucial source that allows us to compare income inequalities both within and between countries around the world.

Still no Play Store, still no Google Services: your phone checks the relay itself, in the background, off by default.
